metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa 250 milestone expansion
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Original distinct questions internally source-checked against pinned implementation evidence. Difficulty is provisional, not player-calibrated or independently approved.
metadata.attribution: GEEK Protocol original questions. Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source is credited per item as primary implementation evidence; no source prose or code is imported.

questions.prompt: When GHOSTDAG chooses between parents with unequal blue work, which parent wins?
options: The parent with the greatest blue work
The parent with the greatest blue score, regardless of blue work
The parent received first by this node
The parent with the latest timestamp, regardless of work
questions.funFact: The reference implementation compares accumulated blue work. Local arrival order does not choose the selected parent.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa, what breaks a SortableBlock tie when blue work is equal?
options: The block timestamp
The block hash
The number of transaction inputs
The peer arrival order
questions.funFact: SortableBlock compares blue work first and then hashes, giving nodes a deterministic comparison when work ties.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does GHOSTDAG parameter K bound when adding blocks to its blue set?
options: The total number of blocks in the DAG
The number of selected parents per block
The blue anticone size allowed for each blue block
The size of the transaction mempool
questions.funFact: The candidate and existing blue blocks must continue satisfying the K-cluster anticone constraints. K is not a wallet or currency setting.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In the topological mergeset order used by GHOSTDAG, how are ancestors placed relative to their children?
options: Children always come before their ancestors
Every block is sorted only by its displayed timestamp
Blocks are placed in local arrival order
Ancestors come before their children
questions.funFact: The implementation describes this order as forward from blocks to children. It respects ancestry rather than a node's reception times.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does unordered_mergeset_without_selected_parent collect in Rusty Kaspa?
options: Blocks reached through other parents that are outside the selected parent's past
All ancestors of the selected parent, excluding other branches
Only the new block's direct parents
Only blue blocks already on the selected-parent chain
questions.funFact: The traversal starts with non-selected parents, walks backward and skips ancestors already covered by the selected parent.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa calculate a new block's blue score from its selected parent?
options: Parent blue score plus the number of mergeset reds
Parent blue score plus the size of the new block's mergeset blues
Parent blue work plus the new block's transaction count
The largest parent timestamp divided by the block interval
questions.funFact: The score recurrence adds a block count, whereas the separate blue-work recurrence sums work represented by blue blocks.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What happens to a regular, non-coinbase Kaspa transaction containing no inputs?
options: It spends directly from the address in its first output
It is valid if its outputs sum to less than one KAS
It fails the no-input validation check
It is treated as coinbase solely because its input list is empty
questions.funFact: The validator requires an input for non-coinbase transactions. A payment cannot create spendable value merely by naming a recipient.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Can one Kaspa transaction list the same outpoint twice as two separate inputs?
options: Yes; if each copy uses a different signature
Yes; if the total output value is below that outpoint's amount
Yes; if the repeated copies have different sequence numbers
No; duplicate input outpoints are rejected
questions.funFact: The validator tracks previous outpoints in a set. Repeating the same reference does not provide another independent UTXO.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How does the pinned Rusty Kaspa validator treat an output worth exactly zero sompi?
options: It rejects that output
It accepts it whenever the transaction fee is positive
It silently removes that output before hashing
It accepts it only as the last change output
questions.funFact: The output-value range check explicitly rejects zero. This rule concerns a native transaction output, not an off-chain token balance.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which output-value condition causes TxOutTooHigh in Rusty Kaspa?
options: One output exceeds the transaction's storage mass
One output exceeds MAX_SOMPI
One output exceeds the sender's chosen fee rate
One output uses a script-hash locking script
questions.funFact: The range check caps each output at MAX_SOMPI; separate checks also guard aggregate values and arithmetic overflow.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What happens if a regular Kaspa transaction tries to pay more value than its inputs provide?
options: It is accepted if the miner includes it in a valid block
It is accepted if every input signature is valid
It fails with a spend-too-high error
The output total is automatically reduced to the input total
questions.funFact: The UTXO-context validator compares total input and output values. A signature cannot authorize creation of the missing native value.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Why can a correctly signed spend of a newly earned Kaspa coinbase UTXO still fail?
options: Coinbase outputs can never be spent
A valid signature must first be registered with a pool
The destination must use the same address as the miner
The coinbase maturity requirement may not be met
questions.funFact: Coinbase maturity compares the entry's block DAA score plus the maturity parameter against the validation point of view.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: For a valid regular Kaspa transaction, how is its native fee obtained?
options: Total input value minus total output value
Total input value minus only the recipient output, ignoring change
The amount in a dedicated fee output to every miner
The transaction payload interpreted as a sompi amount
questions.funFact: The validator derives the fee from the UTXO value difference. Change outputs belong in total outputs when calculating it.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What must hold for the stored storage-mass commitment during Rusty Kaspa UTXO validation?
options: It may be any value above the compute mass
It must equal the storage mass calculated from transaction context
It must equal the transaction's serialized byte length
It must equal the sum of the input and output values
questions.funFact: The validator computes contextual storage mass and rejects a different committed value. The sender cannot freely declare a lower value.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: If a Kaspa input's spending script fails execution, can sufficient input value alone make that transaction pass full validation?
options: Yes; conservation of value is the only check
Yes; a higher fee bypasses the script
No; full validation also requires the input script checks to pass
Yes; the miner may waive the failing script
questions.funFact: The full validation path executes input scripts in addition to checking amounts, maturity, sequence locks and mass.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes transaction validation in isolation from UTXO-context validation?
options: Isolation checks prove the inputs remain unspent
Isolation checks evaluate scripts against referenced UTXOs
Isolation checks establish permanent finality
Isolation checks do not need the referenced UTXO state
questions.funFact: The isolation pass checks the transaction's own structure and ranges. Input values and coinbase maturity need populated UTXO context.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: For a nonzero Kaspa lock_time below LOCK_TIME_THRESHOLD, which kind of condition does Rusty Kaspa use?
options: A DAA-score condition
A timestamp condition
A relative age counted from each input UTXO
A blue-work target condition
questions.funFact: Values below the threshold use a DAA score; values at or above it use time. Zero and maximum input sequences have separate finalization rules.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How is the feerate-threshold check described in the pinned Rusty Kaspa transaction validator?
options: A consensus minimum fee enforced for every block transaction
A mempool Replace by Fee policy check rather than a consensus rule
A rule determining the coinbase maturity interval
A consensus limit on the number of UTXOs per address
questions.funFact: The code explicitly separates this floating-point mempool threshold from consensus checks, even though it runs in the same validation module.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: With Kaspa SIGHASH_ALL, which outputs does the outputs-hash component commit to?
options: Only the output matching the input index
No transaction outputs
All transaction outputs
Only outputs using the current input's script
questions.funFact: The ordinary outputs-hash path hashes every output. Different sighash modes change what the signature commits to.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does SIGHASH_NONE do to Kaspa's outputs-hash component?
options: It commits only to the output matching the input index
It commits to all outputs except the change output
It removes the current input's amount from the signature hash
It uses the zero hash instead of committing to transaction outputs
questions.funFact: The outputs-hash function returns ZERO_HASH for this mode. Other signature-hash components and script requirements still apply.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: When the matching output exists, which output is hashed by Kaspa SIGHASH_SINGLE?
options: The output at the same index as the input being signed
The output with the same address as the input UTXO
The output with the largest amount
The first output, regardless of the input index
questions.funFact: The SINGLE path uses input_index to select one output. It does not choose by amount, address or arrival time.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What changes in the previous-outputs-hash component when Kaspa ANYONECANPAY is set?
options: The current input's own outpoint is also omitted from the full hash
The combined hash of all input outpoints becomes the zero hash
Every output is omitted regardless of the output sighash mode
The transaction lock_time is omitted from the full hash
questions.funFact: ANYONECANPAY omits the aggregate previous-outpoints component. The current input's own outpoint remains in the full signature hash.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Why does Rusty Kaspa cache signature-hash components shared across transaction inputs?
options: To replace signature verification with a single cached transaction ID
To reuse one input's signature for all other input keys
To avoid repeatedly hashing the same shared transaction data
To avoid fetching the referenced output amounts
questions.funFact: The reused-values structures cache common hashes, avoiding redundant work that would otherwise grow quadratically across many inputs.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which previous-output detail is included in Kaspa's Schnorr signature-hash calculation for the input being signed?
options: The current market value of the referenced UTXO
The total number of addresses in the source wallet
The number of peers that relayed the UTXO's transaction
The referenced UTXO's amount
questions.funFact: The signature hash writes the current input's UTXO amount as well as its script public key and outpoint. Signing uses more than a destination string.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does a wallet derivation path such as m/0/1 describe?
options: A route through a hierarchy of derived keys
The route a transaction follows through network peers
The ordered list of a payment's output amounts
The selected-parent path that confirms a payment
questions.funFact: The derivation path is a sequence of child numbers rooted at m. It describes key derivation rather than a network or payment route.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa BIP32 path notation, what does the apostrophe in a child step such as 7' mark?
options: The branch reserved for change addresses
Hardened derivation
The depth of seven blocks required for a payment
A child key that has already signed a transaction
questions.funFact: Child-number parsing uses the apostrophe suffix to set the hardened flag. The visible index remains 7.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Can Rusty Kaspa derive a hardened child public key using only an extended public key?
options: Yes; all child public keys can be derived from any public key
Yes; but only after that child address has received KAS
No; that operation returns an error
Only if the child index is smaller than the account index
questions.funFact: The extended-public-key derive_child implementation rejects hardened child numbers. Non-hardened public derivation is a different operation.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which key material initializes Rusty Kaspa's BIP32 watch account?
options: A list of seed phrases
An unsigned transaction and its fee
The node's pruning-point hash
Extended public keys
questions.funFact: The watch account stores extended public keys and derives addresses for observation. It does not initialize from a seed phrase in this account payload.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Why does the BIP32 watch account's address-range scan include receive and change branches?
options: Funds may be associated with addresses from either branch
Every payment must appear twice in the ledger
Only the change branch can hold confirmed funds
Receive addresses expire after one scan
questions.funFact: The scan combines derived receive addresses with change addresses. Scanning only one branch can omit relevant account UTXOs.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Besides checking the words, what integrity check does Rusty Kaspa perform when parsing a BIP39 mnemonic?
options: It verifies the wallet's current balance
It checks the mnemonic checksum
It verifies the phrase against a registered owner list
It verifies that every word is unique
questions.funFact: The parser reconstructs entropy and compares checksum bits. Passing this check does not prove that a phrase belongs to the intended wallet.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What kind of randomness does Rusty Kaspa require for generating a new mnemonic?
options: A current block hash used without additional secret randomness
A phrase chosen from familiar personal details
Cryptographically suitable random input
A timestamp padded to the required byte length
questions.funFact: The random mnemonic function requires a cryptographic RNG and fills entropy bytes. Predictable public information is unsuitable for new wallet secrets.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Why can the same mnemonic produce a different BIP39 seed when its optional passphrase changes?
options: The passphrase only changes the display name of the same seed
The node salts each new derivation with its current DAA score
The passphrase changes only the checksum of the existing phrase
The passphrase is part of the seed-derivation salt
questions.funFact: Rusty Kaspa builds the salt from mnemonic followed by the passphrase and applies PBKDF2. This differs from a password that only unlocks a local file.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: With identical mnemonic bytes and identical passphrase bytes, what seed does Rusty Kaspa's BIP39 derivation produce?
options: The same seed each time
A new random seed on every call
A seed selected by the connected node
A seed determined by the wallet balance at recovery time
questions.funFact: PBKDF2 is deterministic for fixed inputs. This reproducibility is part of recovering the same key hierarchy.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How many bytes are in the BIP39 Seed value in the pinned Rusty Kaspa implementation?
options: 16 bytes
64 bytes
32 bytes
33 bytes
questions.funFact: Seed::SIZE is 64 bytes, the PBKDF2 output length. Seed bytes are distinct from mnemonic entropy and encoded address payloads.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does Rusty Kaspa's Seed destructor attempt to do to its stored seed bytes?
options: It retains them indefinitely in a global recovery cache
It stores them in the transaction payload before disposal
Zeroize them when the value is dropped
It replaces the array with its public key without erasing it
questions.funFact: The Drop implementation calls zeroize on the seed array. This is a memory-handling measure, not a guarantee that all possible copies are erased.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What additional derivation data does an extended public key retain beyond its public key?
options: The mnemonic entropy and optional passphrase
Only the current address prefix and balance
The private key and every generated signature
Attributes including a chain code and derivation depth
questions.funFact: ExtendedPublicKey stores ExtendedKeyAttrs, including chain code, depth, child number and parent fingerprint. These support hierarchical public derivation.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: For an eligible mergeset blue block with a positive reward, where does Rusty Kaspa direct its coinbase reward output?
options: To the script reported by that blue block
To the current merging miner regardless of that blue block's script
To the first peer that relays the blue block
To the script in the last transaction of the blue block
questions.funFact: The coinbase builder uses each eligible blue block's recorded script and its subsidy plus fees. It does not pay according to token ownership.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Who receives the aggregated reward output collected from mergeset red blocks in Rusty Kaspa?
options: Each red block's original miner receives a separate output
The miner of the current merging block
The original selected parent's miner receives them all
The rewards are always excluded from the coinbase
questions.funFact: The builder collects red rewards and, when positive, pays one output to the current block's miner script. Eligibility affects the amount collected.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: For a mergeset red block outside the DAA set, what does the pinned coinbase builder add to the merging miner's red reward?
options: Its subsidy plus its total fees
Its subsidy only, without fees
Its total fees, without its subsidy
Neither its subsidy nor any fees
questions.funFact: The non-DAA red branch adds total_fees only. The other red branch adds both subsidy and fees.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which value is passed to Rusty Kaspa's block-subsidy calculation to locate the emission stage?
options: The block's transaction count
The miner's chosen timestamp alone
The current mempool feerate threshold
The block DAA score
questions.funFact: calc_block_subsidy uses the DAA score and configured phase/fork parameters to select the appropriate subsidy-table entry.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In the coinbase payload layout, what follows the miner script bytes?
options: Miner extra data
Another mandatory copy of the blue score
The full list of input UTXOs
The selected parent's signature script
questions.funFact: The serializer appends miner extra_data after the script fields. This is payload content and does not grant authority to spend the reward.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: When Rusty Kaspa modifies only miner data in an existing coinbase payload, which leading fields does it preserve?
options: The old script version and old script length
Blue score and subsidy
The old miner script and all extra data
The selected parent and transaction Merkle root
questions.funFact: modify_coinbase_payload retains the two leading u64 fields and rewrites the script fields and extra data afterward.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What must a standard Kaspa P2SH spending signature script supply in addition to its unlocking data?
options: Only the address's checksum
The source transaction's entire block header
The redeem script as pushed data
The sender's extended public key instead of the redeem script
questions.funFact: The P2SH signature-script builder appends the redeem script as data after the supplied signature bytes. The script must match the output commitment.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which hash construction does Rusty Kaspa use when creating a standard P2SH output from a redeem script?
options: SHA-256 with a 32-byte result
RIPEMD-160 with a 20-byte result
BLAKE2b with a 64-byte result
BLAKE2b with a 32-byte result
questions.funFact: The standard builder hashes the redeem script using BLAKE2b configured to 32 bytes before constructing the script-hash locking script.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In a Kaspa 2-of-3 multisig script, what does the 2 specify?
options: The required number of valid signatures
The number of separate receiving outputs
The number of required block confirmations
The total number of public keys in the script
questions.funFact: The multisig builder places the required-signature threshold in the script separately from the list and count of public keys.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which opcode ends the multisig script produced by the Rusty Kaspa ECDSA multisig builder?
options: OpCheckMultiSig
OpCheckMultiSigECDSA
OpCheckSigECDSA
OpEqual
questions.funFact: The ECDSA builder uses the ECDSA multisignature opcode. The separate 32-byte-key multisig builder ends with OpCheckMultiSig.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Does Rusty Kaspa's standard address-extraction helper return an address for every arbitrary locking script?
options: Yes; every byte string maps to a standard address
Yes; it uses the miner address for unrecognized scripts
No; it returns an error for nonstandard script classes
Yes; it hashes every nonstandard script into an address automatically
questions.funFact: extract_script_pub_key_address recognizes specific standard script forms. Failure to extract an address does not by itself describe all consensus validity rules.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What determines which standard locking-script constructor pay_to_address_script uses?
options: The script version from the most recent block's coinbase
The recipient's current balance
The address's position in the wallet's receive list
The decoded address version
questions.funFact: The helper branches between public-key, ECDSA public-key and script-hash address versions. It does not choose by balance or peer state.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which GetInfo response field tells an integration whether a Kaspa node reports itself synchronized?
options: is_synced
server_version
p2p_id
mempool_size
questions.funFact: GetInfo includes a synchronization flag. A reachable RPC endpoint alone does not establish that the node reports a synchronized state.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which RPC request directly asks a Kaspa node which network it is using?
options: GetConnectedPeerInfo
GetCurrentNetwork
GetMempoolEntry
GetBalanceByAddress
questions.funFact: GetCurrentNetwork returns a network identifier. An integration can check this explicitly instead of inferring the network from a server hostname.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which RPC request retrieves unspent-output records associated with a supplied list of Kaspa addresses?
options: GetBalanceByAddress
GetPeerAddresses
GetUtxosByAddresses
GetCurrentNetwork
questions.funFact: The UTXO request accepts addresses and returns entries for them. Unspent does not necessarily mean immediately spendable: scripts and maturity still apply.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How does RpcMempoolEntryByAddress organize transactions associated with an address?
options: Separate confirmed and finalized transaction lists
A single list containing only coinbase transactions
Only the address's aggregate confirmed balance
Separate sending and receiving lists
questions.funFact: The address-oriented mempool model has sending and receiving collections. These are pending-pool records, not evidence of final settlement.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: Which Kaspa RPC call requests information about peers currently connected to a node?
options: GetConnectedPeerInfo
GetPeerAddresses
GetBlockDagInfo
GetCurrentNetwork
questions.funFact: The API separates connected-peer information from stored peer addresses, balance requests and block-template generation.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's fee-estimate API, what are the units of the recommended feerate?
options: Sompi per serialized byte, irrespective of mass
Sompi per gram of transaction mass
KAS per input
Grams per second
questions.funFact: The documented fee-estimate unit is sompi/gram. Here gram measures transaction mass, not physical weight.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: How does an integration use a recommended Kaspa feerate and a transaction's mass to estimate its native fee?
options: Divide mass by feerate
Use the feerate directly as the complete fee
Multiply feerate by transaction mass
Multiply feerate by the recipient's balance
questions.funFact: The fee API documents fee = feerate × mass. The result is in sompi when the rate is sompi per gram and mass is in grams.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.

questions.prompt: What does estimated_seconds in a Kaspa feerate bucket represent?
options: A guaranteed irreversible settlement deadline
The minimum maturity of every coinbase output
The relative lock duration encoded in each input
An estimated DAG inclusion time for that fee-to-mass rate
questions.funFact: The model describes an estimated inclusion time. It is not a guarantee of acceptance or probabilistic finality.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question; Kaspanet Rusty Kaspa source provides implementation evidence.
